**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2022377, Reactome:R-HSA-6798695)

**Proposed mechanism:** ATP6AP2 (HGNC:1572) —DISRUPTS→ lysosomal acidification (GO:0000312); lysosomal acidification (GO:0000312) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); MME (HGNC:7378) —DISRUPTS→ protein processing (GO:0044265); protein processing (GO:0044265) —LEADS_TO→ Spinocerebellar ataxia (HP:0007072). Loss-of-function mutations in ATP6AP2 disrupt lysosomal acidification, leading to intellectual disability. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in MME disrupt protein processing, contributing to spinocerebellar ataxia. Both disrupted pathways converge on fundamental cellular processes affecting neuronal function.

**How to falsify it:** The hypothesis would be falsified if functional studies demonstrate that mutations in ATP6AP2 do not impair lysosomal acidification or that mutations in MME do not affect protein processing in relevant cellular models, or if these genes are found to be functionally independent with no shared downstream effects on neuronal health. _(variant: Identification of common variants (AF > 1%) in gnomAD in the coding regions of ATP6AP2 or MME that are not associated with either disease phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared and distinct molecular pathways affected by ATP6AP2 and MME mutations could reveal common therapeutic targets for neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disorders, or highlight specific interventions for each disease based on their unique downstream consequences.

#### 4. familial juvenile hyperuricemic nephropathy type 2  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.421)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2022377)

**Proposed mechanism:** ATP6AP2 (HGNC:957) —DISRUPTS→ V-ATPase assembly and function (GO:0005811); V-ATPase assembly and function (GO:0005811) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); REN (HGNC:9909) —DISRUPTS→ Lysosomal acidification (GO:0000314); Lysosomal acidification (GO:0000314) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperuricemia (HP:0002152); Lysosomal acidification (GO:0000314) —LEADS_TO→ Nephropathy (HP:0000110); V-ATPase assembly and function (GO:0005811) —BINDS→ Lysosomal acidification (GO:0000314). ATP6AP2 is a subunit of the V-ATPase, critical for lysosomal acidification. Impaired V-ATPase function due to ATP6AP2 haploinsufficiency leads to intellectual disability. REN, a component of the renin-angiotensin system, also relies on proper V-ATPase function for lysosomal acidification, and its loss-of-function mutations lead to hyperuricemia and nephropathy.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of genetic variants in ATP6AP2 or REN in individuals with intellectual disability or hyperuricemic nephropathy, respectively, or demonstration that ATP6AP2 and REN function independently of lysosomal acidification. _(variant: rs752123282 (ATP6AP2))_

**Why it matters:** Targeting V-ATPase function or downstream pathways could offer therapeutic strategies for both intellectual disability and nephropathy associated with mutations in ATP6AP2 and REN.

**Proposed mechanism:** ATP6AP2 (HGNC:14750) —DISRUPTS→ V-ATPase assembly and function (GO:0005810); V-ATPase assembly and function (GO:0005810) —DECREASES→ Renin-angiotensin system signaling (REACT:R-HSA-2172773); Renin-angiotensin system signaling (REACT:R-HSA-2172773) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); REN (HGNC:9947) —INCREASES→ Renin-angiotensin system signaling (REACT:R-HSA-2172773); ACE (HGNC:100) —INCREASES→ Renin-angiotensin system signaling (REACT:R-HSA-2172773); AGT (HGNC:254) —INCREASES→ Renin-angiotensin system signaling (REACT:R-HSA-2172773); Renin-angiotensin system signaling (REACT:R-HSA-2172773) —LEADS_TO→ Renal tubular dysgenesis (HP:0000149). **Why it matters:** Targeting the renin-angiotensin system or its upstream regulators like ATP6AP2 could offer novel therapeutic strategies for both intellectual disability and renal developmental disorders, although the specific directionality of intervention would need careful consideration.
